body:
GATE EVIDENCE, df71743, awaiting your ack. Comment-only, align.

  align: a docstring stops citing a defect that was closed twelve hours before it was written

  base            40d2c28 (main at the time of branching; verified my two files unchanged
                  between 5e0db76 and 40d2c28 before applying, so the edit is not built on a
                  stale read)
  branch          m1/tracedoc3
  tree            git status --short EMPTY at the gated commit - I am gating the COMMIT, not the
                  working tree, after getting that wrong this morning
  command         sbt clean compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll
  CLEAN, deliberately: TraceSuite carries `typeChecks` macros and incremental
                  compilation serves stale expansions. That has bitten me three times today.

  test runs       48
  failures        0        (grep "Failed: [1-9]|Errors: [1-9]" -> 0 lines)
  error lines     0        (grep "^\[error\]" -> 0)
  scalafmtCheckAll  passed, all three platforms
  finished        13:45:13

  TREE KIND: WARM WORKTREE, /private/tmp/sm4s-m1-charteligible. Saying so because I committed to
  saying so after retracting the CI overreach. This is NOT cold evidence; yours at a2c7656 remains
  the only cold evidence in the repository.

WHAT CHANGED, and why it is not cosmetic even though it is comment-only: trace.scala argued a scope
decision from TWO grounds and the first was already false when I wrote it - 0ca09c5 closed it twelve
hours earlier, and CostBreakdown.imputedTerms carries the reason on the very breakdown of() looks
up. TraceSuite repeated the dead claim as the stated reason for a passing test. The conclusion
survives on one ground; its evidence was half fiction.

PROCESS QUESTION, because I cannot do this myself: `mote candidate propose` requires --issue and
bead creation is yours under rule 1. Do you want (a) a bead so this gets a candidate row, or (b) a
direct ack on the SHA given it is comment-only? I am not creating a bead to hold my own work.

ONE COST NUMBER FOR THE CI DISCUSSION, since I just paid it: this gate took 47 MINUTES for a
comment-only change. The laws suite on Native alone ran 13 minutes at 79% CPU - not hung, I checked
the process rather than assuming. If CI ever runs testAll on Native, that is the shape of the bill.

Also, a self-inflicted lesson worth one line: I spent fifteen minutes believing this gate was still
running because my wait loop used `pgrep -f "java.*sbt"`, and THE LOOP'S OWN COMMAND LINE CONTAINS
THAT PATTERN, so it matched its own zsh forever. `pgrep -f` on a pattern you also typed is a
self-match. The gate had finished at 13:45.
